chapter_title: The Theft of the Rimet Cup
title: Hit the Bullseye
subtitle: Taking turns in the maze ... We all have gone past the point of no return.

trails.title: "The Main Course"
trails.description: An clip of earlier news, smells like alphabet spaghetti and gin.

content.text:
To those reading this right now, I wish you would find pleasure in this novel world.
As secondary education has
become more and more
universal, more and more
people started to enrich their
life with better entertainments,
and that's when pop art came into focus. The younger generation no longer cared that much about the abstract art. Instead, they fell in love with lines, colors, and the manifestation of art on the streets.
This is the beginning of a new art. 
If you are willing to put up with some overly avant-garde persons in this new trend, or you can get over with the soap bubbles, art will win on the streets.
Of course, one has to take this to heart: always stay close to the art, but stay away from its artist.

London Review, Opinions, 1965, 12(31A):11{img}

trails.title: Advanced Opportunism
trails.description: Observe, prepare and wait. When you don't have enough variables for the formula you've learnt before, seize every moment before you act.

items.speaker: Wendy
items.text: Woof woof!
The little bulldog holds the newspaper in his mouth and turns round and round in front of his master, as if showing off his trophy.

items.speaker: Charlton
items.text: Wendy! I've told you so many times. No picking up litter on the road!

items.speaker: Charlton
items.text: What have you brought back this time? Open your mouth, ahhhhhhhh!
Charlton gets the newspaper and flips it over and over.

items.speaker: Charlton
items.text: Luckily, there's nothing dirty on it.

items.speaker: Wendy
items.text: Woo ... Woof!

items.speaker: Charlton
items.text: Oh, gosh! It really messed with my head yesterday. I almost forgot something very important.

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Woof woof, woof.

items.speaker: Wendy
items.text: Woof?

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Woof woof.

items.speaker: Charlton
items.text: Whoa!

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Woof woof.
However, bad luck will never end.

items.speaker: Charlton
items.text: Kids, look!

items.speaker: Charlton
items.text: Look what good news our little Wendy has brought home! The Rimet Cup Exhibition starts today!

items.speaker: Charlton
items.text: Now I have a better idea!

items.speaker: Charlton
items.text: How about visiting the Rimet Cup Exhibition this afternoon?

items.speaker: Wendy
items.text: Woof? Woof!

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Woof, woof.

items.speaker: Charlton
items.text: I heard that they would be doing a lottery in the exhibition. The luckiest guy gets full tickets to all the World Cup rounds!

items.speaker: Charlton
items.text: Our little Pickles is definitely the lucky pup, just like every other draw before!

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Woof woof …

items.speaker: Charlton
items.text: Are you not excited?

items.speaker: Charlton
items.text: There's a chance to get an out-of-print signed football there, then we'll have a new toy for our ball game!

items.speaker: Wendy
items.text: Woof woof!
Upon hearing this, the little bulldog in low spirits quickly adjusts like a mature athlete and rubs up against Charlton.

items.speaker: Charlton
items.text: Heh heh heh! Calm down, Wendy. We will have a democratic voting session.

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Woof ... woof.

items.speaker: Charlton
items.text: Now, does anyone not want to visit the Rimet Cup? Raise your paw, please.
The little bulldog rolls about with excitement, while Pickles slowly and firmly lifts his paw.

items.speaker: Charlton
items.text: All right. It's unanimous!
Charlton crouches down and gives Pickles a quick high five.

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Woof woof.
Exhibition Hall
The exhibition hall of the Rimet Cup is alive with visitors.

items.speaker: Young Visitor
items.text: Mum, look!

items.speaker: Young Visitor
items.text: That man, his hand is glowing with colourful light!

items.speaker: Visitor
items.text: Dear, you promised me you won't make a scene when we're outside and no yelling at strange things.

items.speaker: Young Visitor
items.text: Alright, Mum.
Diggers blends in with the bustling crowds. A bottle of coloured liquid with a strong smell is hidden in his hand.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Phew! Security screening passed.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: The warrior of the new era successfully arrives at the final battlefield with his magnificent bubble device.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: They are waiting for a gale.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: This is going to be the critical transition of our time!
The skylight of the exhibition hall is completely covered by black curtains. Instead of daylight, the brighter fluorescent lamps are used.
The windows on the wall are also sealed off, with only a few vents letting the air in.
Diggers wanders around the hall and finally accepts the depressing fact that the security company has arranged everything fairly well.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Bollocks! What is that? The gale outside can't get in!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: A world without airflow is like a pond of dead water. The soap bubbles of a new world can't blow in.
He looks around and changes his mind.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: But, a real artist never loses the guts and grit.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: If everything goes on smoothly, I can blow enough soap bubbles to create an ocean of reveries within half an hour.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: I just need to cover myself ...
Diggers casually puts the bubble device next to the nearest vent. The weak airflow can't even get the fan of the device to turn halfway around.
Like a dying warrior leaving seeds of hope for the brave in the future, he gazes at the security robots that are patrolling over there and takes a deep breath.
Three.
Two.
One.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Puff!
He fearlessly blows one rainbow soap bubble after another towards the crowd.

items.speaker: Passerby
items.text: Hey, look!

items.speaker: Passerby
items.text: How would someone blow bubbles indoors?

items.speaker: Passerby
items.text: *coughs* What a funny smell!
Undoubtedly, the security robots have noticed the commotion here.
They move towards Diggers immediately.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Oh, bollocks! I am exposed in just a minute?

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Ahh, I need to hurry up. These bubbles are far from enough.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Puff! Puff puff!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Pufffff … *coughs*
The security robots are all here.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Hey, hey, hey!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Seriously, you should respect and treat an artist fairly.
This is a battle doomed to fail.
However, the one who makes an intrepid attempt deserves a more valuable reward.

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: Ugh! There you are again, annoying hooligan.

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: I don't think I can understand what you're thinking. Are arcanists all so stupid that you always overestimate yourselves?

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: I am not defeated, Mr. Iverson.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: The fire of art will never be extinguished, just like our craving for Utopia never ceases.

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: Annoying blabber.
The door is locked from the outside.

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: Though I don't know what stupid idea is lingering in your brain, obviously, you just failed again.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Utopia is not stupid, sir.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Without a goal, life would be stuck in the mess of corrupting materials and entertainment!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: I'm sure, soon enough, people will have the courage to speak up and sing for peace and love!

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: I've met a lot of young people like you who chase unrealistic fantasies.

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: Humph! Ignorant and hilarious.
After a brief uproar, Iverson's footsteps fade away.
A long silence falls upon the dark room.
Even the exhaust noise can be clearly heard.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Great! He walked away.
He raises his head, looking at the dust floating around the exhaust vent.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: I've entered the exhibition hall of the Rimet Cup. I can't make any mistakes starting now.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Climbing through ventilation ducts is just a slight sacrifice in order to awaken the rebellious spirit of everyone.
He shuts down the ventilation system nearby and removes the slate from the exhaust vent.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: *coughs* This doesn't look clean at all!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Anyway, at least it's much better than wasting my time in the cage.
Diggers takes a long leap and manages to reach the narrow entrance.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: I can barely see.
He moves forward with difficulty in the dark, but he doesn't notice that something slips out of his pocket.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Oh, my Revery Bubble Solution!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Shoot! It-It's in my eyes. *coughs* Oh, it's itchy.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: *coughs* Bless me, Talia. Hope the efficacy takes effect a bit slower.
TO BE CONTINUED ...
